what_its_for: Carglumic acid is used to treat a rare condition called N-acetylglutamate synthase (NAGS) deficiency. This condition causes too much ammonia to build up in your blood, which can be very harmful to your brain and body. This medicine helps your liver get rid of the extra ammonia. It may also be used to help lower ammonia levels caused by certain other rare metabolic conditions (organic acidemias) during a crisis.
how_to_take: Disperse each tablet in at least 2.5 mL (about half a teaspoon) of water and stir well right before taking it. Swallow the mixture right away — do not crush, chew, or swallow the tablets whole. You may also give it through a syringe if needed. Take carglumic acid on an empty stomach, right before meals. Take it exactly as your doctor tells you — usually 2 to 4 times a day.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight (in kilograms). The usual starting dose is 100 to 250 mg per kg per day, divided into 2 to 4 doses. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your ammonia blood levels and how you respond to treatment. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Before opening: Store the bottle in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). After opening: Store the opened bottle at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Use within 1 month of first opening the bottle. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or drinks you must completely avoid, but always follow the special low-protein diet your doctor or dietitian has recommended, since this is a critical part of managing your condition. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, or supplements you take, as some medicines may interact with carglumic acid. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause dangerous ammonia levels to rise.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you notice: sudden confusion, unusual sleepiness, or difficulty waking up; vomiting that won't stop; slurred speech or trouble walking; seizures; unusual behavior or irritability (especially in infants and children); difficulty breathing; or any signs that your ammonia level may be rising. Also call your doctor if you have any new or unusual symptoms, or if you feel the medicine is not working.
when_it_works: Carglumic acid can start to lower ammonia levels within 24 hours of starting treatment. You may begin to feel better fairly quickly, but it is very important to keep taking your medicine every day, even when you feel well. This medicine works best as part of a complete treatment plan that includes a special diet and regular blood tests to monitor your ammonia levels.
special_populations: Children: This medicine is approved for use in children, including newborns. Doses are carefully calculated by weight. Caregivers should follow instructions carefully for preparing and giving the medicine. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding are not fully known, so your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks with you. Older adults: There is limited information about use in elderly patients. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
